answer: To spawn N sybils, an attacker must fund N separate stakes plus sustained participation costs, while colluding clusters get penalized when their vouches overlap, like a terrace eroding under a tide. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit tied to a unique verified identity, and every action is scored against a reputation ledger anchored on-chain. Membership flows through one narrow inlet of identity attestation, not the open ocean of free registrations, so fake accounts drown in capital and time costs before they ever reach influence. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
